lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: cleaning and laundry systems that scale

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic cleaning and laundry systems that scale task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner thinks about their real household's current cleaning and laundry habits, identifies what tasks exist and how often each needs doing, then designs a rotation system on paper that assigns each task to a person or names a fair method for deciding who does it, without yet trying the system out.
safetyNotes: This is a planning task only; the learner designs a rotation system on paper and does not need to run or announce it during this lesson.
No cleaning chemicals are used or handled as part of this task.
materials: adult-or-local: a list of the rooms and laundry needs in your real household

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l01-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l01-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l01-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l01-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Name one specific way your rotation system could break down (for example, someone forgetting their week, an unfair task split) and one specific rule you added or would add to prevent it.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u02-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: System completeness: At least six specific tasks are listed with a frequency, and every task has a specific person or rotation method assigned. | Realism and fairness of rotation method: The rotation method is specific and named (alternating weekly, fixed assignment, drawing names) with a clear reason for the choice. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner add a backup plan to their rotation system for what happens when the assigned person is unavailable (for example, away or sick) for one cycle.

duration.elapsedWindow: Up to seven days; use only the check-ins explicitly named in the task
duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: cleaning and laundry systems that scale worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner thinks about their real household's current cleaning and laundry habits, identifies what tasks exist and how often each needs doing, then designs a rotation system on paper that assigns each task to a person or names a fair method for deciding who does it, without yet trying the system out.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact cleaning and laundry systems that scale decision or action.
Model move 2: List every cleaning and laundry task your household currently needs, even ones nobody currently does regularly.
Model move 3: Sort your task list into a simple table with three columns: task, frequency, and current person responsible (or 'nobody' if it's not currently assigned).

Model check: System completeness: At least six specific tasks are listed with a frequency, and every task has a specific person or rotation method assigned. | Realism and fairness of rotation method: The rotation method is specific and named (alternating weekly, fixed assignment, drawing names) with a clear reason for the choice.

resources.title: cleaning and laundry systems that scale action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for cleaning and laundry systems that scale.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: cleaning and laundry systems that scale coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner thinks about their real household's current cleaning and laundry habits, identifies what tasks exist and how often each needs doing, then designs a rotation system on paper that assigns each task to a person or names a fair method for deciding who does it, without yet trying the system out.
Coach direction: List every cleaning and laundry task your household currently needs, even ones nobody currently does regularly.
Learner prompt: Write down at least six specific tasks (for example, wiping kitchen counters, vacuuming a specific room, washing towels) and how often each one realistically needs doing.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: cleaning and laundry systems that scale complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Sort your task list into a simple table with three columns: task, frequency, and current person responsible (or 'nobody' if it's not currently assigned).
Response 1 (t2-p1): My table includes at least six tasks with a specific frequency for each (daily, weekly, or a specific number of times per month).
Response 2 (t2-p2): I marked which tasks currently have no assigned person.
Response 3 (t2-p3): Name the two tasks that are least consistently done in your household right now, and explain why you think that is.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: cleaning and laundry systems that scale minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Name one specific way your rotation system could break down (for example, someone forgetting their week, an unfair task split) and one specific rule you added or would add to prevent it.

Success checks: System completeness: At least six specific tasks are listed with a frequency, and every task has a specific person or rotation method assigned. | Realism and fairness of rotation method: The rotation method is specific and named (alternating weekly, fixed assignment, drawing names) with a clear reason for the choice.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: cleaning and laundry systems that scale supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u02-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional cleaning and laundry systems that scale condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — System completeness: At least six specific tasks are listed with a frequency, and every task has a specific person or rotation method assigned. | Realism and fairness of rotation method: The rotation method is specific and named (alternating weekly, fixed assignment, drawing names) with a clear reason for the choice..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

may: coach the guided and retry cards

tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
